question:
**Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.**

A hard nut to crack

options.text: Any subject which several folks are talking about
Something that people believe or accept as true without questioning it
An excessive enthusiasm or rage about a minor matter
A problem that is difficult to solve

solution:
The correct answer is: **A problem that is difficult to solve**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 

 
• The idiom "**a hard nut to crack**" is used to describe a problem that is very difficult to solve or a person who is very difficult to understand. (ऐसी समस्या जिसे हल करना बहुत कठिन हो या ऐसा व्यक्ति जिसे समझना बहुत कठिन हो)

 
 
• **Example**: *Understanding quantum physics can be a hard nut to crack for many students.*
 
 
 
• The word "**nut**" in this context refers to a hard-shelled fruit or seed that is difficult to open.
 
• The idiom can be used in both formal and informal contexts.
 
• Synonyms of this idiom include "a tough nut to crack," "a hard row to hoe," and "a hard pill to swallow."

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 4**.
